findings.claim: TECH-SPEC §6.9's live-e2e.yml row for Codex CLI still lists OPENAI_API_KEY as a required CI secret and a config built from `hooks.json + config.toml [features] hooks = true`, but ADR-0012 (status Accepted, 2026-10-14) explicitly supersedes §6.9 and states Codex runs keyless: it is already logged in with ChatGPT, `codex exec` needs no key, and the real trap is that `--ignore-user-config` still loads the owner's `~/.codex/hooks.json`, so the harness must build a temp `CODEX_HOME` containing only a symlink to `auth.json`. The same class of bug was already caught for Kiro (`KIRO_API_KEY`) and Copilot CLI (PAT) in REVIEW-r4a.md:25,159, but the identical stale row for Codex was not caught — TECH-SPEC.md:362 was never edited after ADR-0012 landed.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:362 '| Codex CLI | required | `codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral` | OPENAI_API_KEY | temp CODEX_HOME with hooks.json + config.toml `[features] hooks = true` |'. docs/v2/adr/0012-live-e2e-keyless-harness.md:3 'Supersedes: TECH-SPEC §6.9 (the CI job with keys)'; same file: '| Codex | it is logged in with ChatGPT. `codex exec` runs with no key, using a temp CODEX_HOME that contains only a symlink to auth.json |' and '| Codex isolation | `--ignore-user-config` still loads `~/.codex/hooks.json` (the owner's v1 hooks), which is why the temp CODEX_HOME is needed |'. Owner decision (core memory, 2026-10-14): 'E2E test istiyorum ... Sonnet low ile en az maliyetle'; ADR-0012 quotes owner directly: 'API key veremem; Claude Code'da çalışan bir harness olursa arada bir kendim çalıştırırım.'
findings.archaeology: ORIGINAL_INTENT (ADR-0012): remove the CI-secret model entirely because the owner refuses to hand out an API key, replacing it with a harness that runs under the owner's own logged-in Claude Code / Codex sessions. REGRESSION_RISK: if §6.9's table is read as still-current spec (it has no strikethrough, no 'superseded' note on the Codex row itself — only the ADR says it supersedes §6.9), an implementer builds the Codex CI job around OPENAI_API_KEY and the wrong flag set (`--skip-git-repo-check --ephemeral`, never mentioned in ADR-0012), silently reintroducing the exact CI-secrets-for-E2E design the owner rejected, and misses the `--ignore-user-config`-still-loads-hooks.json trap that ADR-0012 found live. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no second, undocumented Codex invocation path — one canonical Codex E2E command, matching ADR-0012's temp CODEX_HOME + auth.json-symlink design, with no API key.
findings.fix: Strike or rewrite TECH-SPEC §6.9's Codex row to point at ADR-0012 instead of restating the old key-based design; remove 'OPENAI_API_KEY' and the `hooks.json + config.toml` config description, replacing it with ADR-0012's temp CODEX_HOME + auth.json symlink + `--ignore-user-config` trap. Apply the same strike to every other §6.9 row already superseded by ADR-0012 (Claude Code's row is fine since ADR-0012 restates it; Codex's is not).

findings.claim: TECH-SPEC marks Q11 ('All 10 agents, Codex included, are supported and release-gated by GP-LIVE-ROUTING; no AGENTS.md') as Decided ([D]), but the open spike S-CODEX ('Codex: are MCP tools deferred, and when does the namespace description become visible?') is listed in the same doc's open-spikes table as explicitly blocking Q11. A spike marked open and blocking cannot sit under a question already marked Decided without saying how the gap was closed.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:399 '| S-CODEX | Codex: are MCP tools deferred, and when does the namespace description become visible? | Q11 |'; docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:418 '| Q11 | **All 10 agents, Codex included, are supported and release-gated by GP-LIVE-ROUTING**; no `AGENTS.md` | **[D]** |'; docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:75 '[V] not visible at session start (the probe saw neither; the server log shows `tools/list` was called) ... Whether Codex defers MCP tools: **[U]**'.
findings.archaeology: ORIGINAL_INTENT: GP-LIVE-ROUTING was meant to be the release gate that proves routing quality per agent (§3.1/§7); Q11's 'Decided' status presumes that gate is buildable today, but S-CODEX's [U] means the actual mechanics of Codex tool visibility (deferred loading vs eager) are still unknown, so the GP-LIVE-ROUTING test for Codex cannot yet be written correctly. REGRESSION_RISK: if the release-gating test is built on an assumption about when the namespace description becomes visible and that assumption is wrong, Codex could pass CI while shipping the same silent-routing-failure class the probe was built to catch (§3.1 C2: 'tool descriptions are always sent is false on Claude Code and Codex').
findings.fix: Either resolve S-CODEX before release (read the 37 `defer_loading` references under `codex-rs/core/src` already identified in TECH-SPEC.md:75, confirm live) and drop it from the open-spikes table, or demote Q11 from [D] to [D, pending S-CODEX] so the release gate is not built on an unconfirmed assumption.
